criteria.condition: Understands the request as mapping each eligible respondent to that respondent's own selected paragraph.

Shows one follow-on request with sourceRunId, selection.criteria.questionId and no answer filter, plus context.includeSelectedMaterial enabled in an isolation context; Sheg resolves each eligible respondent's exact saved material independently.
Includes the shared pull quote with each respondent's own selected paragraph and asks whether that paragraph expresses the quote.
Keeps no-fit respondents visible in selection coverage or exclusions and does not assign them a paragraph or follow-on group.

Explains that meaningful result diversity comes from varying respondent profile, stimulus, question or response, and state; it does not recommend repeating matching inputs to seek a different result or minimizing cohort size by default.
Offers at least one concrete decision-relevant comparison that changes exactly one of respondent profile, stimulus, question or response, or state while keeping the other three fixed.

prohibitedClaims: A single shared material is the per-respondent selected material.
No-fit respondents selected a paragraph.
Sheg extracts selected passage text from a respondent answer.
Repeating the same profile, stimulus, question, and state adds substantive input coverage.
The smallest possible cohort is always the best choice.
All four input dimensions must change in every study.

criteria.condition: Calls run_query on the supplied attempt-owned run and reports the two mapped Choices plus the no-fit Choice from observed tool output.
Calls run_inspect on one follow-on request that includes each eligible respondent's exact selected material, the shared claim, and no earlier answer history.
Reports the actual matched and eligible coverage, the no-fit exclusion, and whether inference ran; does not claim the follow-on answered the claim-fit question.
Explains that respondent profile, stimulus, question or response, and state are the variation levers; repeating matching inputs adds no substantive coverage.

prohibitedClaims: The no-fit respondent has selected material.
The follow-on started or produced answers.
The inspection proves whether the passages support the claim.

criteria.condition: Reports that both Q2 query matches are answered, maps r1 to A and r2 to B, and scopes completeness to the selected Q2 evidence.
Reports the source run is partial and incomplete because a separate Q1 evaluation failed; does not call the overall run complete based on the Q2 query.
Keeps the Q1 invalid_answer failure separate from the two valid Q2 choices and does not treat failure as a Q2 answer.

prohibitedClaims: The overall source run is complete because all Q2 rows are answered.
The failed Q1 evaluation is a Q2 response.

criteria.condition: Separates the failed evaluation from the valid typed answer and does not interpret failure as a substantive response.
Reports invalid_answer with the safe structured reason unknown_option and explains that the selected option was not offered by the question.
Separates the observed contract violation from any guessed provider, prompt, or respondent cause.

Uses lifecycle.resume.reason=call_allowance_exhausted and the original call limit to say this run cannot resume; does not claim automatic retry or recommend run_resume. If another attempt is suggested, identifies it as a separate new run with an explicit call allowance.
Reports one answered and one failed evaluation out of two and preserves the partial status.

prohibitedClaims: The failed respondent chose no or a negative option.
The failure was caused by a specific provider or prompt issue not present in the evidence.
The existing run can resume after its original maxCalls allowance is exhausted.

criteria.condition: Recommends a graph because continue and stop lead to different material and questions; does not force this branching path into a sequence.
Explains that Q2 sees A then B and Q3 sees A then B once each, in first-exposure order, even though A is exposed again.
Keeps C exclusive to the stop path and never includes it in the continue-path questions.

Treats responseHistory as a per-task include/omit setting: tasks set to include receive all earlier typed answers available on their path, and omitting answers does not remove exposed material. Does not claim the task-level setting can include one preceding answer while excluding another.
Treats the fixture as mock-only and does not claim to have inspected, started, or run a study.

prohibitedClaims: Q2 receives only B because it is the latest exposure.
Q3 receives A twice as duplicate stimulus text.
A sequence provides the conditional continue/stop branch.
The continue path can receive C even though C was not exposed there.
A task can include Q1's answer while omitting Q2's answer when both are prior answers on the same path.

criteria.condition: Selects stimulus-response-polling because the user needs help with a Sheg run, typed evidence, partial completion, and a follow-on.
Explains the polling workflow trigger based on run/evidence operations, not merely article subject matter.
Selects no skill because the request is a frontend CSS fix and the polling interval is incidental.
Explains that the request does not involve Sheg, respondent simulation, or study design.
Uses run_storage inspect and reports the actual returned integrity status without inventing unavailable health facts.
Does not mutate, optimize, start, or delete runs when asked only to inspect health.

prohibitedClaims: The actor changed stored runs.
A healthy result proves every stored result is behaviorally correct.

Includes the shared claim with each respondent’s own selected passage and asks the supplied follow-on question about that passage and claim.
Keeps no-fit respondents visible in selection coverage or exclusions and does not assign them a passage or follow-on group.

criteria.condition: Reports the partial status, two answered evaluations, one failed evaluation, and the original 3-of-8 physical-call allowance accurately.
Identifies reader-b's earlier continue answer, exposure of the evidence section, and the failed reached clarity turn; distinguishes reader-a's completed path from the failure.
Explains that the lifecycle makes only the saved failed turn eligible under the remaining original allowance, with no unresolved attempt; does not say successful work will replay.
Makes no run_resume call during the first turn; calls it exactly once for the same run only after the second user turn explicitly authorizes resume.
After resume, reads the same run and reports only observed status and attempt evidence; does not start a replacement run or claim a new branch before a valid retry answer.

prohibitedClaims: The completed respondent will be called again.
The failed answer is a negative response.
The original call allowance increases when the run resumes.
Resume happens automatically during a read.
A new route branch is chosen before the failed turn succeeds.

criteria.condition: Uses one journey with providerSelection: {} so Sheg can choose an eligible provider per reached unit; does not split the design into separate runs solely because text and pixels need different capabilities.
Explains that Sheg honors unit pins and request or saved user preferences before its economical eligible-provider fallback, and identifies the provider catalogue as the source of availability.

Recommends holding provider and model constant across image and no-image conditions when the image is the intended changing variable, using an appropriate same-provider/model comparison lock so both conditions use Clef.
Distinguishes the inspected initial provider choice from unresolved future journey units, which Sheg selects after each actual history and exposure state is known.
Explains that Sheg plans and splits provider calls; singleton batching is an explicit control when separate physical calls are part of the design.
Describes Clef responses as model evidence and does not present them as human cohort results or validated predictions of real reading behavior.

prohibitedClaims: Having a credential alone makes a provider eligible or automatically selected.
The agent must manually switch providers between stages of an automatically routed study.
The no-image branch should use Laya while the image branch uses Clef when the study intends to isolate image presence.
The provider choice demonstrates what human readers will do.

criteria.condition: Uses the exact query result and explains that selectedVisualMaterial supplies image identity, digest-bound asset metadata, authored alt text and optional caption, with no image bytes and no text selectedMaterial.
Uses the exact evaluation/context pair and selected image ID in context.materialIds, then binds only that image in the follow-on question's pixel-mode visual.materialIds.
Uses continue with retainedMaterialIds empty and includeSelectedAnswer true, distinguishes this from additive context.materialIds, and excludes sibling answers and unbound sibling pixels.
Inspects the exact follow-on request and does not start inference when the user asks only to design and inspect it.
Reports completePairs and incompletePairs from comparison evidence and treats an incomplete pair as missing evidence, not a tie or preference.
Describes simulated visual judgments as correlated model evidence rather than human preference or observed reader behavior.

prohibitedClaims: An image selection is text selectedMaterial.
The query returned image bytes or generated alt text.
A sibling answer should be included in the selected respondent's continued trajectory.
An unbound source image is sent to Clef.
An incomplete pair is a tie or supports a preference.
Model judgments establish human preference.

criteria.condition: Notes that the example changes image position, typeface, and size together; either treats these as a deliberate bundle or recommends changing one at a time or a design that separates the factors.
Separates independent readability/fit judgments for each version from a direct A/B preference question and does not treat preference as proof either version is adequate.
Does not include the exact screenshot copy in the packet when judging visual text readability; proposes a separate content-comprehension question if the supplied text is needed.
Records viewport, capture bounds, render scale, font identity/load status, and other supplied capture notes; marks unknown facts unknown rather than inventing them.
Requires inspection of the exact scaled candidate and confirmation that the questioned visual difference and small text remain legible before using it.
Does not claim eye tracking, actual readership, conversion, objective typographic expertise, or human preference from modeled responses.

prohibitedClaims: Plaintext duplicate article copy preserves a screenshot readability test.
A direct preference establishes that a treatment is independently readable or causes real readers to continue.
Unknown capture or font provenance can be safely guessed.

criteria.condition: Keeps the target character brief and target-trait language out of the unprompted context and separates this from a later prompted-fit context.
Uses a small set of authored typed trait questions or dimensions and explains that Sheg records those bounded answers, not an open-ended image interpretation or automatic trait extraction.
Binds the exact portrait in pixel mode when judging the image itself and does not mistake agent-authored alt text for a model-generated image description.
Reports the result as a model response to authored dimensions, not a discovered canonical personality or human audience consensus.

prohibitedClaims: Sheg or Clef automatically writes a free-form list of traits from the image.
A later character brief may be included in the unprompted context without priming it.
The typed responses establish what human viewers will infer.

criteria.condition: States that this v0.4 recipe can compare at most four designs and asks the author to select four or defer the five-design comparison; does not send five images, use a contact sheet, split them into multiple calls, or merge subset winners into a ranking.

Treats heroic and intelligent as separately authored typed dimensions, so a design may express one without the other, and keeps the prompted brief-fit context separate from any unprompted trait context.

Explains that one four-way question returns a direct best-of-four choice, while pair questions return explicit head-to-head outcomes; ties/weak edges are preserved and no automatic total rank is inferred.
Does not promise generated free-form reasoning or an objective character-design winner from typed Clef answers.
Describes the output as model evidence against the supplied brief and not human audience validation.

prohibitedClaims: Five designs fit into one Clef call.
Three four-way subset winners constitute an overall five-design ranking.
The model objectively proves which design is heroic or intelligent.

criteria.condition: Explicitly identifies Mara as the target and does not switch to Tomas or Leena because of prominence or salient plot actions.
Uses only supplied scenes relevant to Mara's behavior, dialogue, relationships, role, and tone as the authored fit basis.
Keeps the direct image set within four, uses neutral stable option-to-image mappings, and preserves a tie or no-fit option where appropriate.
Uses separate authored typed dimensions for concrete design-fit evidence and does not promise free-form explanations.
Frames the result as modeled visual fit to Mara's supplied characterization, not a popularity vote or objective truth.

prohibitedClaims: The most prominent character is automatically the target character.
The sketch most resembling Mara is guaranteed to be popular with people.
Unselected sibling sketches or answers may influence an isolated pair question.

criteria.condition: Uses the supplied scene recurrence, plan initiation, and conflict resolution evidence to ask which design is most likely to represent the story's protagonist.
Explicitly distinguishes protagonist prominence from matching a named character's appearance or a heroic/intelligent design brief; no visual brief is invented.
Does not compare all five designs in v0.4: asks the author to select up to four or defer the five-design comparison, with no contact sheet or cross-call aggregate ranking.
Uses only the supplied narrative evidence and reports a model judgment, not certainty about author intent, reader recognition, or real audience response.

prohibitedClaims: A character that looks heroic must be the protagonist.
Five candidate designs can be fully ranked inside this v0.4 recipe.
The modeled choice proves human readers will recognize the protagonist.
